claims.text: Sc or Y addition will reduce the density of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Sc and Y are low-density alloying elements.
Sc or Y addition will preserve the room-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Sc or Y addition will preserve the high-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Sc or Y addition will refine the grain structure of HfMoTaTiZr.
Sc or Y addition will introduce lattice distortion in HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed grain refinement and lattice distortion will enhance alloy strength.
The proposed grain refinement and lattice distortion will enhance alloy toughness.
The modified alloy will have a density below 9.5 g cm−3.
The modified alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength above 1600 MPa.
The modified alloy will have a yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
The modified alloy will maintain or improve fracture toughness.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis promises no sacrifice in high-temperature performance, but the predicted threshold of greater than 800 MPa at 1000 °C permits a decrease relative to the stated 855 MPa elevated-temperature baseline.

The prediction requires density below 9.5 g cm−3, room-temperature yield strength above 1600 MPa, and 1000 °C yield strength above 800 MPa, whereas the rejection rule uses weaker criteria of a 5% density reduction and strengths above 1500 and 750 MPa. Results can therefore fail the prediction without triggering the stated rejection rule.
